summary.name: Electron
summary.one_liner: Electron is an open-source framework for building cross-platform desktop apps with JavaScript, HTML, and CSS, embedding Chromium and Node.js.
use_cases: Building a cross-platform desktop app with web technologies
Shipping automatic software updates to macOS and Windows users
Packaging installers for macOS, Windows, or Linux
Distributing a desktop app through an app store
Collecting crash reports from desktop app users
summary.what_it_does: Electron embeds Chromium and Node.js so developers can write desktop applications in JavaScript, HTML, and CSS, and run them on macOS, Windows, and Linux. Its main process APIs expose operating system features such as window appearance, application menus, dialogs, and notifications. The autoUpdater module (powered by Squirrel) delivers updates on macOS and Windows, and the crashReporter module collects JavaScript and native crash data. Electron Forge is a toolkit for scaffolding, bundling, and publishing apps, and Electron Fiddle is a tool for trying out small experiments that can be saved as GitHub Gists or local folders. Packages from the npm ecosystem can be used, and native add-ons can be written.
notable: Embeds Chromium and Node.js, with major versions released in lockstep with Chromium
Electron Forge toolkit for building and publishing apps
Electron Fiddle for trying small experiments, shareable as GitHub Gists
caveats: Auto-updates are listed only for macOS and Windows users
Installer generation relies on community-supported tooling
